tag: a crash returns an empty insights list again
why: The committed defect. (The first cut of this blind wrote `[] or [{...}]`, which evaluates to the NON-EMPTY list — a no-op that reported the guard VACUOUS when nothing had been restored. A blind that changes no behaviour accuses a guard of its own mistake.) The sole reader takes `insights` and nothing else, so an empty list renders as "Create projects to generate portfolio insights": a crash shown to the founder as the statement that they have no projects. Every other key, `error` included, survives here — which is how the original was.

tag: the failure stops saying that nothing was counted
old: "detail": (f"The computation failed, so this is NOT a statement that you have no "
new: "detail": (f"No insights are available right now. " + f"" + f"" if False else f"No insights are available right now. "
why: A failure named without saying what it is NOT is still read as a measured zero: 'no insights available' and 'you have no projects' are the same sentence to a reader. The whole value of this row's fix is the clause that refuses that reading.

tag: a cap goes back to being a bare literal
why: The writer and the reader must agree on the cap or the reader cannot know what it is counting against. A literal in the writer is how this store dropped rows for rounds while its count read as complete — the number was correct and known to nobody.

tag: the deliverables count stops saying it is truncated
why: A renamed key is silent. The store sits exactly on its cap in normal use, so this is the live case and not an edge one: a total over a store that has been discarding its oldest rows reads as a complete count of everything produced.

tag: the cascade count stops saying it is truncated
why: The same defect in the second store. This route already states its UNREADABLE case out loud ('this is not a statement that you have none') and said nothing at all about a TRUNCATED one — the two absences are the same class and only one was handled.

tag: the governance page stops saying whether the ledger took it
why: The `ledger` string stays computed and is simply not appended — the shape a half-finished fix takes, and the one a source check for the variable name would pass. On the page whose whole purpose is to show that a change was recorded, a filing whose UEG append FAILED then renders identically to one that succeeded.

old:
"status": "CHECKED",
            "detail": (f"{len(external_data)} supplied external signal(s) were mapped to "
new: "detail": (f"{len(external_data)} supplied external signal(s) were mapped to "
why: `status` is the key that tells a caller WHICH path ran, and it was present on one branch and absent on the other — so the caller who most needs it gets undefined precisely when the answer matters. The leg compares the key SETS rather than looking for a string.

tag: a stage announces a start it may never end
new:
yield _ev(f"{stage_key}_start", stage_label, stage_desc)
        prompt_template = prompts.get(stage_key, "")
        if not prompt_template:
            yield _ev(f"{stage_key}_skipped", stage_label,
why: The ORDER is the fix. Even with the skip event present, announcing the start first means a reader watching the stream sees a stage begin before anything knows whether it can run — and an absent ending is indistinguishable from a stream that was cut off. Latent today, because all four engines declare every template.

tag: the compliance dimensions are flattened away again
why: A renamed key, so the chip maps over nothing and renders no dimension gap while the framework row still reads 'assessed'. That is the exact state this row was filed for: the reader can see THAT the framework ran and never that all four dimensions inside it assessed nothing.

tag: the chip stops rendering the dimension gap
why: The producer-side fix is worthless if the surface drops it, and this is the half that would be silently lost: dimGaps is still computed and still correct, and simply never shown. A writer fixed without its reader moves the untruth down a layer.
